title: OpsLace runbook-to-task adapter and safety fabric
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build OpsLace: a lightweight adapter that compiles curated runbook fragments into composable tasklets which can be executed via the admin console, CLI, or the safe sandbox. OpsLace provides a safety fabric (RBAC gating, dry-run simulation, idempotency checks, and circuit breakers), standard input typing for step validation, and built-in telemetry hooks so every admin action emits structured spans and cost/latency metrics. Goal: reduce mean time-to-remediate for common incidents by providing pre-approved, auditable tasklets that non-expert responders can run with one click or via automation triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter compiles at least 8 canonical runbook fragments to typed tasklet JSON schema and stores artifacts in runbook-store
Execution path supports: dry-run, preview diff, and actual run with RBAC checks enforced
Tasklet execution emits structured telemetry (trace id, step durations, token counts) to ops-tracing dashboard
Admin console shows a single-click UI for approved tasklets with parameter form and 'simulate' toggle
CLI wrapper can execute tasklets with --simulate flag and exit codes for success/failure
Safety gates block destructive actions unless canary and approvals are present; automated revert hints are surfaced on failure

notes: Trade-offs: Strong typing reduces user errors but adds friction to authoring new runbook snippets; mitigated by a 'loose' mode for advanced authors and a conversion helper tool.
Performance: JSON schema validation added latency in staging. Plan to move to a compiled validator using generated Rust bindings for hot paths if batching optimization is insufficient.
Safety: Default execution channel is 'simulate' for non-SRE roles. Only service accounts with canary_flag can run destructive steps; all approvals are stored in WORM audit ledger.
Migration: We will publish a migration guide for existing runbook fragments and auto-convert high-frequency playbooks during the first month after release.
